Section-granular arena regeneration for Folia / CanvasMC.

Download `SyncArenas-1.0.1.jar` below and drop it into `plugins/`.

> **Use this release, not v1.0.0.** v1.0.0 was built against the 26.3 API and shipped Java 25
> bytecode, so anything older refused it with `Unsupported API version 26.3`. Nothing in the plugin
> itself changed - it is the same code, compiled against the oldest supported API instead.

## Supported servers

| Server | Status |
| --- | --- |
| CanvasMC / Folia 1.21.11, 26.1.2, 26.2, 26.3 | supported, region threading in use |
| Paper 1.21.11 and newer | supported, one region instead of many |

Compiled against the 1.21.11 API and declaring `api-version: 1.21.11`, because a server only
refuses a plugin whose api-version is *newer* than its own. The jar is Java 21 bytecode, so it loads
on a 1.21.11 server (Java 21) and on 26.x (Java 25) alike. Everything it calls - the region, async
and entity schedulers included - has been in the Paper API since 1.20.1 and is unchanged through
26.3, so there are no version specific code paths.

## Commands

All under the `syncarenas.admin` permission (`op` by default).

| Command | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `/arena wand` | Selection wand. Left click = first corner, right click = second corner. |
| `/arena create <name>` | Snapshots the selection into `<name>.sa` and starts tracking it. |
| `/arena reset <name>` | Restores every section touched since the last reset. |
| `/arena reset <name> full` | Restores every section, dirty or not. |
| `/arena list` | Arenas with size, sections, dirty sections and state. |
| `/arena delete <name>` | Unregisters the arena and deletes its files. |

## How it keeps off the region threads

An arena's pristine state is captured once into a seekable `.sa` file with one deflated entry per
16x16x16 section. Block events do nothing but flip a bit for the section they happened in, so a
reset reads, inflates and rewrites only the damaged sections - 2 dirty out of 5000 stays 2 out of
5000.

- All file I/O, deflate/inflate, palette building and bit packing run on the **async scheduler**.
  Region threads only run the raw block writes, plus one cheap `getChunkSnapshot` per chunk during
  capture.
- A reset is **one work item per chunk**, dispatched through `RegionScheduler` for that chunk, so it
  spreads across every region thread that owns a piece of the arena instead of running on one.
- Each slice writes blocks until `restore.region-budget-micros` (400us default, under 1% of a tick)
  is spent, then resumes on that region's next tick from a stored cursor.
- Blocks are compared before writing (a read costs no light update and no block change packet),
  written with `applyPhysics = false`, and each chunk is held by a plugin ticket while it restores.
- The tracking listeners allocate nothing per event: one reference comparison per loaded world with
  arenas, one union box test, then a packed `long` into a concurrent set. All `MONITOR` +
  `ignoreCancelled`.

Sections that could not be restored (world unloaded, server stopping) go back into the dirty set,
which is persisted into the arena's `.json` on an interval and on shutdown.

`/arena create` and `/arena reset` both report what they did, including the region thread time the
operation actually cost:

```
[SyncArenas] Reset CrystalPvP: 37 sections in 14 chunks, 24,113 blocks rewritten of 151,552 checked
[SyncArenas] Took 212.4ms wall clock, 38.7ms of region thread time in total.
```

## Known limitations

- Only block states are restored; block entity contents (chest inventories, sign text) are not part
  of the snapshot.
- Entities are not touched - dropped items and end crystals are left to your arena logic.
- Blocks are restored without physics, which is what you want for an arena but means a restored
  state is not re-validated against its neighbours.
- `/arena create` captures what is there, so make the selection while the arena is pristine.

## Verification

`mvn verify` gates this release: a clean compile plus 30 server-free tests covering palette bit
packing at every width, section/chunk key packing, arena geometry, the `.sa` writer/reader round
trip (index offsets, refusal of foreign or incomplete files), and the restore walk - every in-bounds
block of every section visited exactly once in payload order, no matter where the budget breaks a
slice. The same suite was run against both the 1.21.11 and the 26.3 API.
